raised.quote:
if (!allowedKeys.has(verdict.new_issue_key!)) { skipped++; continue; }
      pushInto(byKey, verdict.new_issue_key!, verdict);
raised.claim: Verdicts attached to a new issue are not checked against that issue's scope.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal scoped to candidates_count > 0 can be created with a zero-candidate verdict; the issue is published and the row linked even though the same attachment would be rejected on the next run.

raised.quote:
if (scope.beer_ids.length > 0) return true;
  return scope.where.some((t) => t.col !== 'review_class');
raised.claim: Adding any beer ID bypasses the prohibition on whole-class scopes.
raised.why_it_breaks: A scope with beer_ids [1] and where review_class = matcher_bug is accepted, and its where branch subsequently accepts every matcher_bug row, recreating the whole-class dumping ground.

raised.claim: The saturation check ignores other rows already accepted in the same plan.
raised.why_it_breaks: If an issue has 11 post-creation rows and a batch proposes five more, every verdict sees 11 and all five are attached, exceeding the limit of 12.

raised.claim: Model-authored issue prose can override the structured scope that is appended after it.
raised.why_it_breaks: If issue.body contains an earlier triage-scope fence, parseScopeBlock selects that first block on the next run, returning its scope or null instead of the rendered structured scope.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: Saturation counts disappear when linked failure rows are cleared or reopened.
raised.why_it_breaks: After 12 examples have been commented on an issue, matching those beers deletes their failure rows, and a candidate-count transition clears reviewed_at. The count falls below 12 even though the examples remain on the issue, allowing further attachments.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: Text comparison misorders timestamps with and without fractional seconds.
raised.why_it_breaks: GitHub supplies created_at like 2026-08-14T06:00:00Z while the job writes reviewed_at like 2026-08-14T06:00:00.500Z. The latter is chronologically later but compares lexically smaller, so an attachment in the same second is not counted.

raised.quote:
`UPDATE enrich_failures
         SET review_class = ?, review_note = ?, reviewed_at = ?, issue_number = ?
       WHERE beer_id = ?`,
raised.claim: The new issue link is not cleared when a failure is reopened for triage.
raised.why_it_breaks: When candidates_count crosses the zero boundary, recordEnrichFailure clears the review class, note, and timestamp but leaves issue_number intact. The now-untriaged row still appears linked to its former issue in queries using the new authoritative column.

raised.quote:
UPDATE enrich_failures
     SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
   WHERE review_note LIKE '%→ #%'
     AND CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER) > 0;
raised.claim: The migration backfills the first issue reference in a note rather than the appended routing reference.
raised.why_it_breaks: A review note such as 'related to → #123 → #456' was routed to #456, but instr selects #123. The migrated link and saturation count are assigned to the wrong issue.

raised.claim: Guard hits are not logged when the model supplies a verdict for every row.
raised.why_it_breaks: Coverage counts proposed verdicts before guards run. If all rows have verdicts but all violate scope, covered equals the batch size and no verdict-shortfall log reports the repeated guard failures.

raised.claim: Degraded absence verdicts are reported as wontfix in the triage digest.
raised.why_it_breaks: The job increments wontfix for every quiet verdict other than not_on_untappd. A candidate-bearing absence verdict is now changed to matcher_bug and stored as such, but the digest reports it as wontfix.

raised.claim: Appending the scope after unrestricted prose can hide it from subsequent triage prompts.
raised.why_it_breaks: When the model-authored body exceeds the 2,000-character prompt cap, the appended scope is omitted from the next prompt. The model can then propose attachments without seeing the condition that the deterministic guard will enforce.

raised.claim: The strict tool schema permits column and operator combinations that the analysis parser rejects.
raised.why_it_breaks: For example, a tool response with col 'candidate_count' or an unsupported operator satisfies this JSON schema but fails ScopeSchema validation, causing the whole analysis batch to fail instead of rejecting only the bad proposal.
